homelessClaims.claim: authoritative_state action providers for the 'source-release', 'package-publish' and 'deployment' release kinds
homelessClaims.requiredBy: DECIDE-SETTLEMENT-RELEASED via PROD-PUBLICATION/PROD-OBSERVATION (settlement requires a trusted authoritative_state receipt+observation for EVERY required action of the declared policy kind)
homelessClaims.gap: missing product obligation, not missing test evidence: the repository ships exactly one production provider kind (source-tag via saga-local-git-release); the default composition explicitly throws delivery-provider-not-configured and documents that real publication must be supplied by a deployment-specific override that does not exist in this repository. A truthful 'released' whose policy declares source-release/package-publish/deployment actions therefore has no in-repo producer for its required effect/observation evidence.

safetyClaims.claim: candidate-drifted: settlement compares input.currentCandidateHash and observation.currentCandidateHash to the certified candidate; the local provider independently re-observes commit/tree; changed hash after certification blocks release

every delivery snapshot is hash-verified against its self-declared hash and its durable reference (preflight/approval/publication/observation/releaseRecord/certificate); mismatch is terminal 'failed', never released

untrusted or unmatched providers (preflight/approval/action/observation) yield blocked verdicts; trust requires an active trusted_providers row matched on id+name+category+version; no default provider exists

every action execution observes the provider first and skips mutation when the desired state already matches; the effect ledger + deterministic actionKey make retries idempotent across runs; a push/command response alone never establishes release
release adapters must not force push, bypass branch protection, registry immutability or deployment policy; the local provider creates tags via compare-and-set update-ref against the zero OID

human approval binds candidate+preflight+policy hashes and cannot float to a later revision; recorded decisions are immutable (replay-divergence throws); a pending approval pauses rather than fabricating consent

no externally-visible release action may begin without an explicit operator grant bound to the immutable policy hash and a candidate scope (lifecycle-output or exact hash); executeAction re-checks the grant

terminal fields are write-once: ProcessRun outcome/output/certificate; LifecycleRun terminal_status (completeStage rejects already-terminal stages and enforces the lease CAS); ReleaseRecord persisted once with hash re-check; non-'released' decisions must not expose a record
the default local-dry-run composition throws a typed failure at the publication boundary; the port type admits only success shapes so no code path can synthesize a released outcome from it
Delivery emits a local outcome only; cross-module routing authority belongs to the lifecycle definition, preventing the release module from grading its own conveyor position
launch claim/running transitions are CAS-fenced by claim_token; one active launch per order; spawn is acknowledged only by the durable lifecycle start receipt, never by OS success

development settlement reads only exact accepted CandidateSet/revision products; execution ids are provenance; Kanban tasks are never settlement authority — preventing latest-execution material selection from poisoning the certified candidate

livenessClaims.claim: a pending approval pauses the ProcessRun/LifecycleRun truthfully; the operator records the immutable decision and resumes the SAME run, which re-enters the human node and replays the decision; approval-required is a terminal business outcome when never decided, with the continuation path as the lawful suffix

process settlement routes only under a fenced in_progress transition obligation; the reconciler re-drives idempotent lifecycle episodes so a committed child result is eventually routed or surfaces a typed pending pause
competing terminal paths (dispatch and obligation re-drive) converge to one run.terminal event via a durable claim; a lost observation line never becomes a broken run

delivery node completions are durable; crash-resume restores the chain from NodeRun rows, accounts for failed rows in the crash window, detects same-reason spin, and bounds the walk by a seeded step budget

ProcessRun and LifecycleRun execution leases are acquired/renewed with heartbeats; lost leases surface typed errors instead of silent double-ownership; the lifecycle transition budget fails cycles distinctly

auditClaims.claim: factory_process_transitions stores every stage transition with outcome, target and terminal_status plus handoff/decision hashes — the durable routing evidence for the released verdict
ProcessOutcomeCertificate rows (authority 'delivery_settlement_policy' / development settlement) are the content-addressed verdict records referenced by ModuleCompletion certificateRefs

the run.terminal envelope separates outcome/status (operational), terminal_status (business verdict), stage_outcome(+authority) and product_outcome — no channel implies another; exit codes never flatten the verdict

the ReleaseRecord enumerates every observed destination (actionKey, kind, target, externalRef, observedStateHash) — the canonical released-state audit artifact, re-readable by exact process-run identity
the external-effect ledger retains per-action execution/observation snapshots, attempts, fences and states — reconstructing the idempotency history behind each receipt

uncertainties: No in-repo UI/API mints an authorized operator grant for a fresh launch: the direct path relies on a caller-supplied lifecycleInput (repo-root fixtures such as autism-buttons-lifecycle-input.json / hex-lifecycle-input.json demonstrate the shape); the in-repo producer is only prepareLocalReleaseContinuation. This is treated as the intended external operator boundary, not a homeless product obligation, because the input contract enforces the grant's presence and binding.

PROD-OBSERVATION completeness trusts providers.observeCurrentCandidateHash: a provider returning a stale-but-matching hash could weaken the drift check; the local-git provider re-derives it from the branch head, but other future providers must preserve that discipline (no production provider for non-source-tag kinds exists yet — see homelessClaims).

The reverse walk stops at module settlement boundaries for Discovery/Formalization internals: only their outcome contracts and handoff mappings are prerequisites of 'released'; their internal cell loops are structurally identical to Development's (same production-cell executor) but were not independently expanded.

tests/factory-evidence/delivery/delivery_happy-released-authorized.json records a complete durable 'released' run through the real product-delivery lifecycle (authorized mode, source-tag style deployment action) — used only as corroborating existence evidence; no live database was inspected (out of scope).

dep-18 names the Development 'verified' route as the predecessor of the delivery handoff; the id prefix 'OUTC-DELIVERY-RELEASED-predecessor:' is an annotation for the reverse ordering, not a claim id.
